messages:
maya: Quick design check — putting together options for form error surfaces on Settings > Model Pins (see Figma link). Inline errors vs top summary + focus, required markers, and delete-confirm copy. Thoughts? dan: +1 for seeing all three options. can you paste the small screenshots here? mobile behaviour especially matters. maya: pasted two screenshots and a short gif. Options: 1) inline only (errors next to fields, red outline), 2) top summary + inline anchors (summary lists errors, fields keep inline hints), 3) summary only (for compactness). Also debating required: red asterisk vs trailing "(required)" copy. sophia: my vote is 2) summary + inline anchors. summary is great for screen readers + keyboard users — we can `role="alert"` / `aria-live="assertive"` for the summary and move focus to it on submit. anchor links from summary -> field = nice affordance. oliver: Agree with summary active. Inline is still useful for context when user scans form later. Also prefer explicit "(required)" — a11y: color alone is not enough. marco: Quick note on destructive confirms: For deleting a model pin I think we should use a typed confirmation when the action can't be undone (e.g., "type DELETE to confirm"). For less risky deletes, a confirm modal + keyboard focus trap is fine. maya: @marco what's the threshold for typed confirm? any heuristic? marco: If deletion affects customer data or billing or removes many records (X > 10) — typed confirm. Also any marketplace/public model removals. Otherwise modal + checkbox "I understand" is okay. maya: Copy tweak suggestions: summary header should be "Please fix these fields to continue" not "Errors" (so less scary). For typed confirm text: "Type DELETE to permanently remove this model pin." keep it short. dan: small a11y nit: when validation fires, ensure `aria-invalid="true"` on fields and that the summary has `aria-describedby` linking to fields. Also set focus to the summary region so screen readers announce list. a11y-bot: Reminder: per WCAG, avoid relying solely on color to indicate required state. Contrast check: the red outline needs to meet 3:1 for UI components. See: https://example.com/contrast-checker sophia: UX note re: inline vs summary for long forms — if validation shows >3 errors, expand summary by default and collapse inline hints to avoid noisy page. perhaps animate focus scroll. oliver: Interaction detail: clicking an item in summary scrolls and sets focus to the input, not the label — helps keyboard users. Also add `data-error-id` so logs tie back to eval prompt sets. maya: Implementation question: should we auto-scroll to first invalid field or to summary? I lean summary first, then user can jump. dan: summary first is common. Implementation: focus summary, then `tab` lands on first field anchor. for mobile, scroll directly to the first inline error because summary can be off-screen. marco: Edge case: server-side error on save (500) — show a non-blocking toast + keep inline fields highlighted. If it's a validation error from API, map the server field errors into the summary. maya: Okay consensus forming: adopt option 2 (summary + inline anchors), explicit "(required)" labels, typed confirms for irreversible deletes, focus summary on desktop, scroll-to-first-inline-on-mobile, and WCAG contrast + aria attributes. I'll update Figma and write a short spec for engineering. sophia: thanks! could you add a short example snippet for the summary region? I can pair on accessibility review. maya: snippet I plan to add: ```html

Please fix these fields to continue

  • Model name is required
  • Pin count must be a number
``` oliver: perfect. please include the `data-test` attrs too. maya: will do. I'll post the updated spec in ~30m. :thumbsup:
